correctness.rationale: Direct independent-column character sums establish a=-1/(q^d-1) and b=1/((q^d-1)(q^(d-1)-1)) for all finite fields. Rook contrast decomposition yields exactly 1+d^2 eigenvalue dimensions and the 2x2 coupling. Positivity is proved algebraically including the q=d=2 boundary. The determinant comparison has sign d*u^2*((4-d)+(6-2d)t-(d-2)t^2) and establishes dimension-four upper mode transition. A direct checker independently enumerated six instances and passed.

Full primary statements for the closest related sampling results on determinant-one 2-by-2 matrices and rank-one matrices were inspected: their point sets, Fourier bands, and spectra differ; an indexed symplectic-group summary concerns another variety and do not imply the full all-dimensional theorem, although determinant-one matrices over F_2 include the already-covered d=2 q=2 special case. The value/novelty claim concerns the full all-parameter spectrum, not the input sums or this single specialization. Residual equivalent-formulation risk is recorded.

value.rationale: The set GL_d(F_q) is the canonical invertible stratum of the finite-field matrix space; the stability of all first-coordinate Fourier modes is a natural harmonic sampling invariant. The theorem provides its complete uniform spectra, exact best/worst Riesz constants, unexpected universal optimizing-mode transition at d=4, and asymptotic tightness at fixed q. This is neither a single-parameter table nor a restatement of Delsarte rank-character sums.
